title: Invalidation & cache writes
objectives: Choose `invalidateQueries`, `setQueryData`, `refetchQueries`, `resetQueries` or `removeQueries` by what each does to the data on screen, to staleness, and to active vs inactive queries
Write query filters that reach exactly the intended entries: a prefix, `exact: true`, `type`/`refetchType` and a `predicate`
Write cached data immutably with `setQueryData`/`setQueriesData` updaters, and explain why an in-place edit leaves the screen unchanged
Decide when to write a response straight into the cache and when to invalidate, and predict what an awaited `invalidateQueries` waits for

questions.prompt: A rename's response contains the full updated todo. Which call shows it in the open detail view **without another request**?

options.text: `queryClient.setQueryData(todoKeys.detail(id), updatedTodo)`
`queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: todoKeys.detail(id) })`
`queryClient.refetchQueries({ queryKey: todoKeys.detail(id) })`
`queryClient.resetQueries({ queryKey: todoKeys.detail(id) })`

questions.explanation: `setQueryData` writes the value synchronously and makes no request; components reading that key re-render with it. The other three all end in a fetch: invalidation marks it stale and refetches it because it's on screen, `refetchQueries` refetches it outright, and `resetQueries` first drops it back to its initial state (a spinner, without `initialData`) and then refetches.

questions.prompt: The open-todos list is on screen; the done-todos list is cached but not mounted. You call `invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['todos'] })`. What happens to each?

options.text: The open list refetches now; the done list is marked stale and refetches when it's next shown
Both refetch now — invalidation refetches every query that matches the key
Only the open list is affected; queries without a mounted component are skipped
The open list refetches now; the done list is removed from the cache to free memory

questions.explanation: Invalidation marks **every** match stale (overriding `staleTime`) and, with the default `refetchType: 'active'`, refetches only the matches a component is using. The done list keeps its data, marked stale, and refetches when a component mounts it again. Refetching both now is `refetchType: 'all'` (or `refetchQueries`); nothing is ever removed by an invalidation.

questions.prompt: A logout handler calls `queryClient.removeQueries()` and only then navigates away, so for a moment the dashboard is still mounted. What does that dashboard do?

options.text: It keeps the old data on screen (it isn't told), then hard-loads if it re-renders before unmounting
It switches to its loading state at once, because the data it was rendering is gone
It re-renders with `data` undefined and `status: 'success'` until something refetches
It throws on its next render, because its query no longer exists in the cache

questions.explanation: `removeQueries` deletes cache entries without notifying their observers, so the screen keeps rendering what it had. On its next render, `useQuery` finds no entry, creates a fresh one and fetches — a hard load, possibly as the logged-out user. That's why v5 removed `useQuery`'s own `remove()`. Navigate away first, then clear the cache.

questions.prompt: A **Refresh** button calls `queryClient.resetQueries({ queryKey: todoKeys.lists() })`, and users complain the table flashes a spinner. Why, and what fits better?

options.text: Reset puts the lists back to their initial `pending` state before refetching; invalidation refetches behind the table
The call isn't awaited; `await queryClient.resetQueries(...)` keeps the old data until the refetch finishes
`staleTime` is 0, so every refetch is treated as a first load and shows a spinner; raise it
`todoKeys.lists()` is too broad and resets every list; reset only `todoKeys.list(filters)` instead

questions.explanation: Reset means "back to how this query started". With no `initialData`, that is no data at all, so the component renders its pending state until the refetch lands. Invalidation keeps the data and fetches in the background (`success` + fetching). Awaiting changes when *your* code resumes, not what the component renders, and `staleTime` doesn't make background refetches show spinners.

questions.prompt: `queryClient.setQueryData(['todos'], (old) => { old.push(newTodo); return old; })` runs while the list is on screen. What happens?

options.text: The cache holds the new todo, but the list doesn't re-render: `data` is still the same array
The list shows the new todo: `setQueryData` always notifies every component reading the key
It throws, because data in the query cache is frozen in development builds
The write is skipped, because the updater returned the same value it was given

questions.explanation: The array was changed in place, so the cache really does contain the new todo — but `useQuery` re-renders a component only when a result field it reads has changed, and `data` is the very same reference. The screen stays stale until something else re-renders it. Cached data isn't frozen, and the write isn't skipped (only an `undefined` return is). Return a new array: `(old) => [...(old ?? []), newTodo]`.

questions.prompt: After creating a todo you want every cached list marked stale, the lists on screen refreshed now, and hidden lists refreshed only when they're shown. Which call?

options.text: `invalidateQueries({ queryKey: todoKeys.lists() })`
`refetchQueries({ queryKey: todoKeys.lists() })`
`invalidateQueries({ queryKey: todoKeys.lists(), refetchType: 'all' })`
`refetchQueries({ queryKey: todoKeys.lists(), type: 'active' })`

questions.explanation: That's exactly invalidation's default (`refetchType: 'active'`). `refetchQueries` matches inactive lists too (its `type` defaults to `'all'`) and fetches them all now, as does `refetchType: 'all'`. `refetchQueries` with `type: 'active'` refreshes the visible lists but marks nothing stale — with a long `staleTime`, a hidden list is shown later *without* the new todo.

questions.prompt: When does `await queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: todoKeys.lists() })` resume?

options.text: When the active matches it refetched have settled — even if one of them failed
Immediately: invalidation only marks queries stale, and refetching happens in the background
Once every matching list, active and inactive, has been refetched
Once the active ones have succeeded; it rejects if any refetch fails

questions.explanation: The promise waits for the refetches it started — by default only the active matches; inactive ones are only marked. Failures are swallowed unless you pass `{ throwOnError: true }` as the second argument, so "awaited" does not mean "fresh": after a failed refetch, `data` is still the old value. Returning this promise from a mutation's `onSuccess` is how a save stays pending until the list is refreshed.

questions.prompt: A rename's response has the updated todo, but lists are sorted by title **on the server**. What should the cache update do?

options.text: Write the detail with `setQueryData`, and invalidate the lists — only the server knows the new order
Patch the row in every list with `setQueriesData`; no request is needed
`invalidateQueries({ queryKey: todoKeys.all })`, which covers the detail and the lists
Nothing: the default `staleTime: 0` refetches everything on the next render

questions.explanation: You hold the exact new detail, so write it. A row patch is right only when the change can't move the row; a server-side sort can, so let the server recompute the lists. Invalidating `todoKeys.all` also refetches the detail you could have written for free. And stale data doesn't refetch on render — only on a trigger (mount, focus, reconnect, invalidation).

prompts.prompt: Patch the saved todo into every cached list, immutably, leaving entries without data alone.
prompts.explanation: `setQueriesData` takes filters and runs the updater on each existing match. `map` returns a new array with a new object for the changed row, so components reading `data` see a new reference; `old?.` returns `undefined` for an entry with no data, which leaves it untouched.

prompts.prompt: The mutation response is the full, updated todo. Put it in the detail entry without a request.
prompts.explanation: `setQueryData` writes one key synchronously and counts as a fresh fetch (`dataUpdatedAt` is now). If no entry exists yet, it creates one — a cheap way to prime a detail page.

prompts.prompt: Mark only the bare `['todos']` entry stale — not the keys under it — and don't refetch anything now.
prompts.explanation: `exact: true` turns the prefix match into an exact one. `refetchType: 'none'` keeps invalidation to its first half — marking stale — so the entry refetches on its next trigger instead of now.

prompts.prompt: Invalidate every todo query except details, with a check the key prefix can't express.
prompts.explanation: `predicate` receives each `Query` and returns whether it matches; with no other filter, it runs against every query in the cache. Reach for it only when a prefix can't say it — a well-shaped key factory usually can (`todoKeys.lists()`).

code: const { data } = useQuery({ queryKey: ["list"], queryFn: async () => ["a"] });
// <Todos /> has rendered "a". Then, from a button elsewhere:
snippets.question: What does the console show, and what does the paragraph show afterwards?
snippets.answer: The console logs ["a", "b"], but the paragraph still shows "a"
snippets.explanation: The push changed the cached array itself, so reading the cache shows both items. But the updater returned the same reference, and `Todos` reads only `data` — unchanged as far as `useQuery` can tell — so it isn't re-rendered. Run headlessly against v5.104, the paragraph stayed at "a"; the immutable version `(old) => [...(old ?? []), "b"]` re-rendered it at once.

code: // ["todos", "open"] is on screen; ["todos", "done"] is cached but unmounted.
// Each has fetched once: fetchCount is { open: 1, done: 1 }.
snippets.question: What are the two logs?
snippets.explanation: Invalidation marks both stale but refetches only the active one (default `refetchType: 'active'`), and its promise waits for that refetch. `refetchQueries` uses the plain filter defaults — `type: 'all'` — so it fetches the unmounted list too. (Run headlessly against v5.104.)

code: const { status, data } = useQuery({ queryKey: ["me"], queryFn: fetchMe });
// …a moment later, the user clicks the paragraph.
snippets.question: What does the paragraph show right after `removeQueries`, and right after the click?
snippets.answer: Still "success: Ada" after removeQueries; after the click, "pending:" while a new fetch runs
snippets.explanation: `removeQueries` deletes the entry without notifying its observers, so nothing re-renders and the old data stays on screen. The click's re-render makes `useQuery` look up `["me"]` again, find nothing, create a fresh entry and fetch it — `status` is `pending` with no data. That's the "hard loading state with the next re-render" the v5 migration guide warns about. (Run headlessly against v5.104.)
